statements.quote: Without adequate safeguards, including both screening and traceability processes, malicious actors could use advances in AI to develop potentially dangerous pathogens and biological weapons.
statements.context: Ossoff's own letter asking whether the administration has replaced the rescinded framework for screening orders of synthetic DNA and RNA, given the risk of AI-assisted bioweapons.

statements.reason: He states in his own words that AI advances could let malicious actors develop pathogens and biological weapons, a catastrophic risk, without extinction framing.

statements.reason: Treats advanced AI as a serious danger needing lab inspectors and a treaty and links it to bioterrorism, but does not spell out a catastrophic consequence of AI in this passage; it sits between C and B.

notes: All six required web searches have now run: three in the first run and the three that were refused then (superintelligence / Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act, extinction or existential risk, and "AI safety") in a second run on 11 November 2026. This is absence of evidence, not a verified 'did not co-sponsor': the Sanders office summary (https://www.sanders.senate.gov/wp-content/uploads/Ban-Artificial-Superintelligence-Act-Release-Summary.pdf, opened) names only Sanders and Rep. The extinction / existential risk search returned no result that mentions Ossoff. UNDATED STATEMENT LEFT OUT OF `statements` (reviewer may want to add it once dated): a Grabien video clip page, 'Sen. Ossoff on AI Regulation: I've Been Very Aggressive in Investigating the Risks to Children' (https://grabien.com/story?id=609188, opened, page text read directly), gives a machine-made 'rush excerpt' transcript in which he says: "That, with artificial intelligence technology can be used to produce seriously dangerous new viruses and pathogens that pose a serious threat to human health and United States and to global health. This is one of the most serious concerns that arises." This would be level B (AI-enabled pathogens, in his own spoken words), the same level and subject as the June letter. It is left out because the page shows no date, programme or interviewer, and the brief requires the date the statement was made; it is also an automatic transcript with visible errors, so the wording should be checked against the video. From its content (he refers to his synthetic DNA inquiry and to preliminary data from the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children, which his office publicised on 6 August 2026) it is probably from August or September 2026, possibly the MS Now interview of about 14 September 2026, but that is a guess. Political Wire, 15 September 2026 (https://politicalwire.com/2026/09/15/ossoff-warns-trump-wont-address-ai-safety-concerns/, opened) only relays the NewsNation / The Hill report already noted below, quoting him: "They've invested heavily in AI labs. They've invested heavily in data centers." That is about the president's conflict of interest, level D at most, and is left out. The NewsNation and The Hill pages themselves returned 403 in the second run, so that interview's full wording was not read. Carried over from the first run: the Atlanta Journal-Constitution page is paywalled: only the one quote used here was readable in the page text; the rest of his rally remarks are scrambled in the page, and an automated summary's reconstruction of them (for example that Trump 'is compromised', that AI company chiefs should testify under oath, that Congress 'sleepwalks' into a technological revolution) was NOT verified and is left out. The rally date of 13 September 2026 is inferred from 'Sunday' in an article updated Monday 14 September 2026. Left out as not about catastrophic risk (level D at most): PBS/Associated Press, 15 September 2026, quoting him at the same rally: "What fills us with dread is the crushing weakness of our politics against the massive stakes of our times" (https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/tech-ceos-call-for-ai-regulation-trump-and-congress-are-not-rushing-to-act); and The Hill via NewsNation, about 14 September 2026, quoting him on MS Now saying the Trump family has invested in AI labs and data centers and that "the president of the United States is compromised" (https://www.newsnationnow.com/business/tech/ai/trump-ai-regulation-jon-ossoff/). The letter's quote of the industry open letter ('there is a real possibility that the knowledge barriers ... will meaningfully erode') is others' words and was not used.
